original_question: For random n x n band matrices H with bandwidth w <= n and independent entries H_ij inside the band, can one prove the Fyodorov-Mirlin conjecture that the local eigenvalue statistics are in the GUE universality class when w is much larger than sqrt(n), but become Poisson when w is much smaller than sqrt(n), in both the real symmetric and complex Hermitian settings?
target_in_paper: Problem 2 (universality for random matrix theory (RMT)), specifically the random-band-matrix paragraph stating the Fyodorov–Mirlin conjecture and the putative critical threshold w ~ sqrt(n).
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the main object and claim very well: random n x n band matrices, bandwidth w, the Fyodorov–Mirlin sqrt(n) threshold, the delocalized/random-matrix side for w much larger than sqrt(n), the Poisson side for w much smaller than sqrt(n), and the fact that the paper explicitly says the conjecture is of interest in both the real symmetric and complex Hermitian cases.
missing_details: The paper explicitly defines the band condition as H_ij = 0 whenever |i - j| >= w.
Inside the band, the paper says the entries are iid; your draft says only independent.
Because of symmetry, independence is only meant for the independent matrix entries (for example one triangle plus the diagonal), not literally all H_ij simultaneously.
The surrounding context of Problem 2 is universality on the microscopic/local scale, so the intended statement is about local bulk eigenvalue statistics rather than edge behavior.
To make the asymptotic regimes fully sharp, 'w much larger than sqrt(n)' and 'w much smaller than sqrt(n)' should be stated as w/sqrt(n) -> infinity and w/sqrt(n) -> 0.
The paper is informal and does not spell out normalization, centering, or variance conventions for the in-band entries; a fully formal theorem statement would need those conventions fixed.

The paper also does not formally define what precise notion of 'GUE' or 'Poisson' local statistics is intended (for example spacing statistics, correlation functions, or another standard local-statistics formulation).
This arXiv paper is an open-problems survey and does not contain Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3; the closest official formulation is this paragraph in Problem 2.
refined_question: Let H = (H_ij) be an n x n random band matrix with bandwidth w <= n, defined by H_ij = 0 for |i - j| >= w, and with the independent in-band entries iid, subject only to either real-symmetric symmetry H = H^T or complex-Hermitian symmetry H = H*. Can one prove the Fyodorov-Mirlin conjecture that the microscopic bulk eigenvalue statistics undergo a transition at the scale w ~ sqrt(n), namely: if w/sqrt(n) -> infinity then the local eigenvalue statistics are of GUE type, whereas if w/sqrt(n) -> 0 then the local eigenvalue statistics are Poisson?
justification: This paper is an informal survey of open problems, so the nearest paper-faithful target is not a numbered conjecture but the random-band-matrix paragraph inside Problem 2. That paragraph matches your draft almost verbatim: it considers n x n band matrices with H_ij = 0 outside the band, states the Fyodorov-Mirlin conjecture with the critical scale sqrt(n), gives the GUE-versus-Poisson dichotomy, and explicitly says the problem is relevant in both the real symmetric and complex Hermitian settings. The surrounding text in Problem 2 makes clear that the intended scale is local/microscopic universality and places the problem in the broader localization-delocalization picture for random Schrödinger operators.
